subject: Request: retro metering rollup & invoice adjustment for ACME Software
messages:
From: Katie Holmes <katie.holmes@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Joshua Walters <joshua.walters@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected March metering spike — request for retro bill review

Hi Evelyn,

We noticed a ~4.3x spike on the AWS Marketplace metering charges for March compared to our February baseline (SKU: redwood-infer-std, Order ID 98765). Per our records usage patterns didn't change and most of the delta looks like high-volume token counts on a single ingestion job. Can you help validate whether these were billed correctly and, if not, advise on a retro invoice adjustment or credit?

We urgently need: the raw metering events (time-windowed), any seller-side corrections you can make, and a timeline for resolution — our finance team needs an answer before the 4/20 close. I attached the ACME February vs March ledger export we pulled from our side (see attachment reference).

Thanks,
Katie Holmes
Head of Procurement
ACME Software

Attachment stubs: ACME-ledger-202703.csv (referenced)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Holmes <katie.holmes@acme.com>
Cc: Joshua Walters <joshua.walters@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected March metering spike — request for retro bill review

Hi Katie — thanks for the clear note and the ledger export. We're on it.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I'll pull the seller metering events for the Order ID 98765 and cross-check with the SKU events (redwood-infer-std).
- Finance (Aditya) will do a quick estimate of potential credit exposure; Ops (Marcus) will advise on whether a rollback or merchant-side adjustment is appropriate.
- We'll open an AWS Marketplace case to validate metering ingestion on their side and request retro adjustments if their logs corroborate an overcount.

Can you confirm whether it is acceptable for us to apply any credit directly against ACME's April invoice (preferred) or if you require a retro-issued invoice/credit note? We want to align with your AP process.

I'll attach the raw export we pulled internally shortly and loop in Laura for invoicing. Expect a follow-up by EOD tomorrow with the initial EV.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199

Attachment stubs: acme_order_98765.pdf (order)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: ACME March usage — initial triage and actions

Team — internal note and action items (not to be shared externally yet):

Summary:
- ACME flagged a 4.3x March spike on SKU redwood-infer-std (Order 98765). Their ledger shows large token counts mostly between 2027-03-14 and 2027-03-16.
- Hypotheses: double-ingestion during a retry storm, delayed aggregator re-emit from our collector, or AWS metering ingestion duplication.

Action items:
1) Marcus: run seller-side metering audit and export events by hour for 2027-03-01..2027-03-31. Compare event count and total tokens vs what was forwarded to AWS. Please attach redwood_marketplace-usage-dump-202703.csv when done. (ETA 4/14 EOD)
2) Aditya: quick FTE exposure estimate and propose credit range (low/likely/high). Include currency breakdown, tax/VAT treatment for credit. (ETA 4/14 noon)
3) Laura: prepare template for credit note + proposed message to ACME if we can credit April invoice vs retro invoice. Note AP preferences for ACME (net-45).
4) Evelyn: open AWS case and push for metering ingestion logs and any known late-arrival duplication.

Ping me with interim artifacts. I'll coordinate comms once we have the AWS case ID.

Thanks,
Evelyn

Quoted earlier: "We noticed a ~4.3x spike on the AWS Marketplace metering charges for March..."

From: aws-marketplace-billing@amazon.com <aws-marketplace-billing@amazon.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Latoya Jenkins <latoya.jenkins@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 07:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Case 123456 — investigation into metering ingestion for seller redwood.ai (Order 98765)

Evelyn,

Thanks for opening Case 123456. Our ingestion team reviewed the Order 98765 events and identified two ingestion batches that overlapped during a replay window on 2027-03-15 UTC which resulted in duplicated metering records for a short period. We have the following next steps: 
- We've isolated the duplicated event IDs and can reject the duplicates at the billing ingestion layer.
- To process a retro adjustment we need a seller-provided CSV of canonical usage (timestamp, event_id, sku, quantity, tokens) for the affected period and a signed seller attestation that the file is authoritative.
- Once the seller CSV and attestation are uploaded to the case, we will schedule a billing reprocess and issue a retro credit or adjusted invoice (processing typically completes in 7-10 business days depending on queue).

Reference: AWS Case 123456 (internal ticket ID).

Regards,
Marketplace Billing Support
Amazon Web Services

Attachment stubs: aws_case_123456.txt

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Holmes <katie.holmes@acme.com>
Cc: Joshua Walters <joshua.walters@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected March metering spike — proposed remediation and timeline

Hi Katie — quick update and proposed remediation path.

What we found:
- AWS confirmed duplication during a replay window on 2027-03-15 and have asked us to provide canonical seller usage for the affected window (they flagged duplicated event IDs).
- Our audit (attached) shows the duplicated events equal ~63% of the reported March overage for Order 98765.

Proposed remediation:
1) We will produce the seller canonical CSV for AWS (redwood_marketplace-usage-dump-202703.csv) and the required attestation and upload to the AWS case by 4/15 EOD.
2) AWS will reprocess and, if approved, issue a retro credit. They estimate 7-10 business days from our upload.
3) To avoid affecting your cash flow while AWS processes the case, Redwood is prepared to apply an interim provisional credit of USD 28,500 to ACME's April invoice (we estimate the final credit will be in the USD 25k–32k range; Aditya will finalize). We will either net-settle this provisional credit against April or replace it with the official AWS credit once issued (with any delta invoiced/credited).

Questions for you:
- Is applying a provisional credit to April acceptable, or do you require a retro-issued credit note for March?
- If provisional credit is acceptable, do you require a formal purchase-order amendment or is an emailed acceptance sufficient for your AP team?

We've attached the audit export and the seller CSV draft for your review. We'll also generate a credit note template for your records.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_marketplace-usage-dump-202703.csv (draft), provisional-credit-note-template.pdf

From: Katie Holmes <katie.holmes@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Joshua Walters <joshua.walters@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected March metering spike — proposed remediation and timeline

Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick investigation and the clear remediation plan. ACME is fine with Redwood applying a provisional credit to the April invoice while AWS completes the reprocess — that helps our month-end. Please proceed.

For audit purposes we do need a retro-issued credit note when the AWS credit is finalized (our auditors require a document referencing the original March invoice). An emailed acceptance is sufficient to proceed with the provisional credit; we'll expect the formal credit note within 30 days of the AWS reprocess completion.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Katie Holmes
Head of Procurement
ACME Software

Attachment stubs: ACME-AP-instructions.pdf
